domain: UN-system procurement: tender notices and contract-award notices across UN organizations
prediction_question: The lead probed was UNGM (United Nations Global Marketplace), the common procurement portal of the UN system - the only substantial un-probed case-grain register in this tick's region. The plausible task family was tender-level: at the publication instant of a UN organization's procurement notice, predict an observable award-side outcome (e.g. whether the DSB-style award lands within N months, whether the tender is cancelled, or award-value attributes), with complainant-analogue features (organization, country, UNSPSC category, notice type, deadline). The session closed the lead on licence grounds before any task probing: the portal's own terms prohibit redistribution of exactly the records a task would ship.
prediction_time: Would have been the publication instant of a tender notice (or the award notice's own date for award-side targets) - never reached: the licence triage (step 1 of the order of work) closed the source first.
target_definition: Would have been an award-side observable (award occurrence/timing/cancellation) - never reached. Recorded only so the shape of the closed lead is documented; the verdict is a licence rejection, not a task finding.

sources.name: UNGM - United Nations Global Marketplace (www.ungm.org), the official procurement portal of the UN system; UNGM Secretariat with UNOPS as service provider since 2008 (UNOPS HQ Copenhagen). Publishes tender notices, contract award notices and LTAs for 40+ UN organizations and entities.
sources.api: Pages reachable anonymously (terms page HTTP 200, 114,147 B, fetched 2026-11-06; award pages render server-side). No documented anonymous bulk/API channel was needed or probed: the licence closed the source first. The Knowledge Centre documents that some UN orgs publish via UNGM web services/API, but the terms govern the Site's Materials regardless of channel.
sources.license: UNGM Terms & Conditions (fetched 2026-11-06): 'Materials' are DEFINED to include requests for proposals, invitations to bid, procurement notices, notices of cancellation AND 'Notices of award'. Clause 5.2: downloads allowed 'for their personal use only'; 'None of the material on the Site may be used for any commercial or public use, and no part of such material may be reproduced or stored in or transmitted to any other website.' Clause 5.3: 'No material on the Site may be disseminated in any form, either electronic or non-electronic, or included in any retrieval system or site without the prior written permission of UNGM.' Clause 7.2: procurement-opportunity Materials 'is copyrighted by these organizations. It may not be reproduced, stored, transmitted or photocopied in any form or by any means without the prior written consent of the respective organizations.'
sources.access: Public pages; award notices accessible free of charge per UNGM's own help centre. Access was never the blocker.

measurements.task_probes_deliberately_not_run: No task-shape, schema or volume probing after the class D instrument was read. Cost of this rejection: 4 direct fetches plus searches.

rejection_reason: Licence class D: the publisher's own terms define 'Materials' to include the tender notices and notices of award a derived dataset would redistribute, then grant only personal-use downloads, prohibit any commercial or public use, prohibit dissemination 'in any form' and inclusion in any retrieval system without prior written permission, and condition reproduction of procurement-opportunity records on the respective UN organization's prior written consent. The administering organization's own instrument (UNOPS Terms of Use) carries the same prohibition for its channels, so there is no clean sibling channel today. Under the standing policy we build only on sources that are already clean: closed, not parked.
next_action: None - closed on licence grounds. Re-open only if (a) a UN organization attaches an explicit open licence (e.g. CC BY) to its own procurement/award data channel - UNGM's clause 7.2 delegates copyright to the individual organizations, so a single-org open-licensed awards channel would be a NEW candidate with its own discovery cycle - or (b) the operator records a candidate-specific risk acceptance (a risk acceptance, never a grant). TASK-SHAPE caveat carried into any reopen: even licence-clean, UN award data shares the measured WB-procurement defect (at-award schema without post-award outcomes = pipeline-continuation hazard, wb-procurement-contract-awards 2026-11-03), so a reopen must name a post-award outcome family with documented timing, not just a different licence.

licence_note: Class D on the publisher's own instrument: UNGM Terms & Conditions clauses 5.2/5.3 (personal use only; no dissemination in any form without permission) with 'Materials' defined to include notices of award; clause 7.2 conditions reproduction on the respective UN organization's written consent.
